FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DOCUMENT. The materials, laboratories and measurements below are invented for software testing.

Bubble detachment on porous nickel electrodes at high current density

Summary. Gas bubbles that remain attached to porous electrodes block active area and raise the cell voltage. We imaged bubble detachment on nickel foam electrodes with a high-speed camera.

Results. At 500 mA cm-2 in 1 M KOH at 60 °C, the mean bubble departure diameter on untreated nickel foam was 180 micrometres. A hydrophilic coating reduced the departure diameter to 70 micrometres and lowered the cell voltage by 45 mV.

Relevance. Electrode wetting and bubble management can change apparent catalyst performance at high current density. Catalyst comparisons at high current should therefore state the electrode substrate and any surface treatment.

This study did not test CM-2, LX-4 or RT-1.
